title: IRDAI Chairman Ajay Seth: Reshaping How You Buy Insurance
description: IRDAI Chairman Ajay Seth is leading major reforms in how insurance is sold in India. The regulator plans to change how insurance agents and distributors are p.

faq.a: Mis-selling happens when an insurance policy is sold to a customer by providing incorrect information, hiding important details, or recommending a product that is unsuitable for their needs, often driven by the seller's desire for higher commissions.

faq.q: Will these changes affect my existing insurance policies?
faq.a: The proposals are primarily for new policies and the future conduct of agents. While the exact impact on existing policies isn't detailed yet, the overall aim is to improve the industry's standards, which could indirectly benefit all policyholders through better service and accountability.

faq.q: When will these new rules come into effect?
faq.a: IRDAI is expected to release a consultation paper by the end of July 2026. After receiving feedback from various stakeholders (like insurance companies, agents, and the public), the final regulations will be drafted and notified, which could take some time.

faq.q: How much compensation can I get if I'm mis-sold a policy?
faq.a: The IRDAI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, which came into effect on July 1, 2026, allows for compensation up to ₹30 lakh for consequential losses and up to ₹3 lakh for loss of time, expenses, harassment, and mental anguish in cases of deficiency in service.
